key_insight: The model’s materials-science knowledge is not just stored in hidden states; it is also encoded in how states transform and can be causally steered to change answers.
engineering_relevance: This suggests language models can be probed and controlled for mechanism-aware scientific reasoning, which could improve trust, debugging, and targeted prompting in materials engineering workflows.
method: Read hidden-state concepts with direct and Jacobian vocabulary readouts.
Test whether state movements align with physical laws using counterfactual, direction-reversed prompts.
Use causal interventions and state patches to shift answer probabilities and transfer decision signals.
evidence_signal: In 50 held-out descriptions, three Jacobian lenses reproduced concept ranks and blinded readouts identified 9 of 10 mechanism families; a 72-prompt benchmark and 60-law counterfactual test further showed 39 of 40 directional laws were correctly oriented.
watch_item: Some apparent structure in hidden-state neighborhoods may reflect numerical similarity rather than true physical organization, so causal checks are needed before interpreting internal geometry as mechanism understanding.
paper_title: Reading and Steering Representations of Materials-Science Mechanisms in an Open-Weight Language Model
